key_insight: Physical danger in embodied-agent plans is not the same as text-level unsafe content: the two signals are separable in LLM hidden states, enabling better safety detection beyond keyword-based moderation.
engineering_relevance: For robotics and agent systems, a lightweight hidden-state probe can reduce false alarms on benign instructions while catching physically risky plans more reliably than standard LLM judges.
method: Analyze hidden-state directions to test whether content danger (CD) and physical danger (PD) are distinct.
Train PRISM, a single-layer L2-regularized logistic probe on full hidden states.
Validate with random-split null tests and cross-benchmark evaluation on SafeAgentBench, PSB-1K, SafeText, and EARBench.
evidence_signal: Across Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B, Phi-3.5, and SmolLM2, PRISM reached 86.2–87.7% accuracy on SafeAgentBench and 99.6% on PSB-1K, while same-scale LLM judges showed much higher false positives on safe tasks.
watch_item: Because PRISM relies on hidden-state probing, performance may depend on model architecture, layer choice, and distribution shift to new embodied tasks or unseen physical domains.
paper_title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
